correctness.rationale: For every uniform labeled associative quasitrivial operation, the known unique ordered-partition projection structure makes K exactly the sum of binomial(block size,2). This yields the exact marked EGF. Nonnegative coefficients at mark 1 yield a unique simple dominant pole; the Fourier-marked series is entire in z for real t, so a uniform one-pole expansion and implicit differentiation give mean, positive variance and CLT. For the large tail, a fixed density of tied pairs forces a linear-size total mass of giant blocks, costing at least the square-root threshold in factorial weights, and a single block attains that exponent. Direct multiplication table checks corroborate the exact finite formula. Formal convergence and fixed delta bounds are respected.

value.rationale: The noncommuting-pair count is an intrinsic semigroup invariant and has a complete finite law that explains two genuinely distinct asymptotic scales: a linear Gaussian bulk and a superexponentially unlikely positive-density event whose n log n rate is sharp. This resolves quantitative behavior not captured by enumerating whole classes or fully commutative extremes. The sharp rate identifies giant weak-order blocks as the only leading-order mechanism.
